question: _____________ and ___________ are called as narrow and broad money, respectively, in the context of money supply in an economy.
solution:
The correct answer is__** M1 and M3 **__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• In macroeconomics, the money supply refers to the total volume of currency held by the public at a particular point in time.
 
• **M1 and M3** are called as narrow and broad money, respectively, in the context of money supply in an economy.
 
• There are several ways to define "money", but standard measures usually include currency in circulation and demand deposits

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• M1, M2, and M3 are measurements of the United States money supply, known as the money aggregates.
 
• M1 includes money in circulation plus checkable deposits in banks. 
 
• M2 includes M1 plus savings deposits (less than $100,000) and money market mutual funds.
 
• M3 includes M2 plus large-time deposits in banks.
